content: A common notation in QFT is the Dirac slash operator, e.g. "slash D". Not sure $\not\!D$ will show it correctly... Any suggestions on whether this notation can be (or should be) approximated in lean somehow?

This seems to work, but I don't know if it is valid or how we can make it easy to write: 

import Mathlib

variable (p : ℕ)
def slashed (x : ℕ) : ℤ := x
notation x "̸" => slashed x
#check p̸

At least for me in VS-code the slash appears over the p.

I assume you had to copy paste it in or something and there isn't a text shortcut. I would be hesitant to use notation which doesn't have a text shortcut, or at least have another option. Thinking of alternate notation, maybe use \quot to get the slash without confusing with division?
Yeah - I had to copy and paste, but was hoping that there was an easy way to define custom text shortcuts, but maybe this isn't the case.
Is the question just how to add new unicode shortcuts to VSCode? You can place it in .vscode/settings.json under lean4.input.customTranslations.

Awesome! Thanks @Chris Henson . Just checked that adding: 

"lean4.input.customTranslations": {
      "slashed" : "̸"
    }

to the .vscode/settings.json does indeed replace e.g. \slashed p with p with a line through it etc.
